newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rising sea may threaten Maldives in 2060s - minister.
newsitem.headline: Rising sea may threaten Maldives in 2060s - minister.

text.p: The Maldive Islands could be seriously endangered in 70 years by rising sea levels caused by global warming, Maldivian Foreign Minister Fathullah Jameel said on Friday.
"The worst scenario is that in 70 years, the sea will rise to a level where the slightest storm will flood the country," Jameel told a news conference at the end of his three-day visit to Sri Lanka.
"But this does not mean we will be completely submerged. Attention is been given to the problem. We will keep on talking about the issue to sensitise the world to it over the years," he said.
Jameel said he hoped for some solution in future technology.
The Indian Ocean archipelago of 1,192 islands is said to be in danger as global warming causes sea levels to rise around the planet. The islands have a population of 245,000.
Jameel joked he had sought a solution for the problem from his counterpart in the mountainous Himalayan kingdom of Bhutan.
"I asked the Bhutanese foreign minister 'why don't I give you an island and you give me a mountain'," Jameel said.
